answer:
Calculate the Darcy-Weisbach pressure drop for water flowing through a horizontal galvanized-iron pipe.
Pipe length is 100 m, internal diameter is 50 mm (0.05 m).
Volumetric flow rate is 2 L/s (0.002 m³/s).
Water temperature is 20 °C, density is 998 kg/m³, dynamic viscosity is 1×10⁻³ Pa·s.
Absolute roughness of galvanized iron is 0.15 mm (0.00015 m).
The pipe is horizontal, so no elevation head loss is included.
Compute the mean flow velocity from Q and the pipe cross-sectional area.
Compute the Reynolds number using ρvD/μ.
Compute the relative roughness ε/D.
Determine the Darcy friction factor f using the Colebrook-White equation (iterative) or an equivalent Moody-chart read for the given Re and ε/D.
Apply the Darcy-Weisbach equation ΔP = f (L/D) (ρv²/2) to obtain the pressure drop in pascals.
Report the final pressure drop in kPa to one decimal place, and state the intermediate values (velocity, Reynolds number, friction factor) used.
